Collage Capsules: Build a Mini Bookshelf or Exhibit

Join us for an afternoon of FREE community crafting and imaginative making with the Palo Alto Library!

Transform an Altoid tin into your own miniature bookshelf or exhibit using vintage-inspired collage materials, trinkets, and unique ephemera. Patrons will leave with a one-of-a-kind keepsake that tells a story in miniature.

This hands-on creative workshop is presented in partnership with the Palo Alto Library. All are welcome, but best suited for teens and adults. 

All supplies are provided; no experience necessary.

Janet Lansbury with Ruth Whippman

 
 

Janet Lansbury, the go-to parenting expert behind the #1 podcast Unruffled and author of No Bad Kids, joins us with her essential guide to caring for, understanding, comforting, and bonding with infants and toddlers.

About the Book 

Most parenting books focus on what to do with and for your baby. Baby Person invites you to consider how you see your child in the first place: rather than a blank slate you must mold and shape, your baby is a thinking, expressive person, capable of being in relationship with you from birth. In pioneering infant and child expert Janet Lansbury’s warm and eminently helpful hands, this is more than just an ideology; Baby Person makes it actionable.

Drawing on the central tenets of the RIE (Resources for Infant Educarers) philosophy, as well as Lansbury’s thirty-plus years working with families and being a parent herself, Baby Person gives parents the tools to deal confidently with the pressure points they face every day—from helping a child sleep peacefully and eat readily to encouraging them to accept and even appreciate boundaries. With sound advice on everything from tantrums to potty training, Lansbury guides caregivers through these early years with tools that alleviate anxiety and promote joyful connection, giving parents the permission to worry less and enjoy the relationship—and their role in it—more.

A guide sure to be cherished by readers everywhere, Baby Person will reframe the way a whole generation relates to the young people in their lives, becoming the calm and emotionally present caregivers they want to be now and beyond the tender first few years.

About the Speakers

Janet Lansbury is a parenting teacher and consultant whose blog is read by millions annually. Her podcast, Janet Lansbury Unruffled, is one of the all-time most downloaded parenting podcasts. Trained by Magda Gerber in her Resources for Infant Educarers (RIE) philosophy, Lansbury has more than thirty years of hands-on experience working with parents and their infants and toddlers. The author of No Bad Kids and Elevating Child Care, she lives in Los Angeles with her husband, with whom she has three grown children.

Ruth Whippman is a British author, journalist, and cultural critic living in Berkeley. A former BBC documentary director and producer, her writing has appeared in the New York Times, Time magazine, New York magazine, The Guardian, HuffPost, and elsewhere. Fortune described her as one of the “25 sharpest minds” of the decade. Whippman is the author of America the Anxious, which was a New York Post Best Book of the Year and a New York Times Editors’ Choice, and BoyMom: Reimagining Boyhood in the Age of Impossible Masculinity.

ACCESSIBILITY: We never want cost to be a barrier to admission for our community. Please email events [at] keplers [dot] org if you would like to attend this event but cannot afford a ticket. To request an accommodation under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) for this event, please email events [at] keplers [dot] org at least one week prior to the event.

REFUND POLICY: All ticket purchases are final. We are unable to offer refunds for this event.

We want Kepler’s to be a welcoming and comfortable space for everyone. If you are feeling unwell, especially with respiratory symptoms, please stay home. Thank you for helping us create a safe and considerate environment for our community.

Existence Beyond Death : With Dr. Seng-Beng Ho - Friday November 6th at 7pm

Existence Beyond Death
Scientific Evidence for Near-Death Experiences, Reincarnation, and the UFO Connection

A Conversation with Dr. Seng-Beng Ho - Author & Cognitive Scientist


Hosted by Julie Kalua

• Limited to 25 participants

Cost: $25

Live event at East West Bookshop · This event fills quickly — register early
Live event here at East West Bookshop

For ages 15 and older.

Powered by

What might near-death experiences, reincarnation, and UFO encounters reveal about consciousness—and the nature of reality itself?

Join Dr. Seng-Beng Ho for an evening exploring these three subjects and their possible connections. Drawing from his book, Science and Sensibleness: An Intellectual Survival Guide for the UFO Age, Seng-Beng will examine research and reported experiences that he argues challenge a purely material understanding of consciousness.

The presentation will move from near-death experiences to reincarnation, then explore the UFO connection, including reported telepathic communication and similarities between some encounter accounts and near-death experiences.

Designed for curious newcomers as well as those already exploring these questions, the evening will include a roughly 45-minute presentation, followed by Q&A and time for attendees who wish to share their own experiences.

Limited copies are available on our New Books table. Books will also be available for purchase before/after the event.

Please arrive 10–15 minutes early to allow time for parking and check-in.

Ticket & Cancellation Policy

All ticket sales are non-refundable. Because seating is limited, your registration represents a commitment to attend and reserves a space specifically for you.

If you are unable to attend, please contact Julie before the event. Your registration may be transferred to another person or, when applicable, the ticket value may be applied as a credit toward a future event. All transfers and credits must be arranged in advance by email.

If the event is canceled by the organizer, ticket holders will receive a full refund. Send requests to julie.eastwestbooks@gmail.com

About Julie Kalua

Julie Kalua is a sound practitioner, educator, and buyer for East West Bookshop’s singing bowl department. With years of experience selecting and working with bowls, she brings a finely attuned ear for tone, resonance, and subtle shifts in the nervous system developed through direct practice and community offerings.

Through workshops, private sessions, and one-on-one mentorship, Julie guides participants in building a more grounded relationship with their bodies using sound, breath, and simple embodied practices. Her work centers on steadiness, internal alignment, and giving people practical tools they can carry into daily life.

Sound remains her primary medium — not as performance, but as a resource for presence, clarity, and self-trust.
